# `terrain-slam`

Scenario kind of the engine v0.39.0, family [GPS-denied alternative PNT](../gps-denied-alternative-pnt.md). Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service. Every label here is the engine's or the verification matrix's; a kind is MODELLED unless the matrix says otherwise (how a label is earned: the README's Evidence section).

## What it does

GPS-denied sequential (recursive) terrain-referenced navigation: a particle filter runs the terrain-match measurement model epoch by epoch (SITAN as a running filter) so a time-varying INS drift is tracked along the track, where the batch terrain-nav only recovers a single constant offset.

One run of `scenarios/terrain-slam.toml` summarises as: terrain-slam | 60 waypoints | free-inertial RMS 2947 m (final 5082 m) | terrain-matched RMS 1241 m (final 69 m, 2x cut) | mean ESS 2599/4000 | matching sigma 17.0 m

## Evidence

No matrix row names this kind by name; the label on its result is the engine's own, above.

The rows the run itself exercised, with the oracle the matrix gives each (the public sources are named there):

- **MODELLED** Gravity-map matching, terrain-referenced (TERCOM/SITAN), magnetic anomaly. Oracle (InternalConsistency): IGRF-14 coefficients; first-principles matched-filter CRLB. The real-field gravity benchmark's field is externally checked (row 'Gravity-anomaly synthesis from a spherical-harmonic model'), but its navigation outcome has no external oracle
- **MODELLED** Deterministic, scenario-hashed, SBOM + cross-platform golden gates. Oracle (ExternalDataset): SBOM conformance to the official CycloneDX 1.5 JSON Schema (+ valid SPDX identifiers) — an external published standard, zero validation errors over the full dependency graph; the FoM-determinism / byte-reproducibility part remains a pinned self-consistency check, so the row stays MODELLED
